correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=1, arbitrary full-dimensional centrally symmetric equators, h>0, and 0<=t<=1, reflection-overlap sections reduce by the Brunn–Minkowski midpoint argument to the same horizontal center. The three exact axial integrals are valid throughout [-t,1], including separate direct endpoint arguments; their signs identify precisely one maximizing c, and substituted algebra yields the stated ratio. Direct log differentiation, parameter inversion, centroid integration and the binomial inequality prove all accompanying results. A new standalone checker from the present package passed 570 independent exact-rational cross-section integrations and 25 numerical shifted-cube tests; those finite tests are supplementary only.
residual_risks: No external independent mathematical verification has been performed.

originality.rationale: The explicit all-dimensional maximal point-reflection volume, its base-shape independence, location formula, monotone inversion and high-dimensional limit are not stated or implied by the relevant primary materials inspected. Stein 1956 establishes universal uniqueness and simplex cases, which are credited and excluded from novelty. Chakerian–Stein 1965 supplies general bounds, Huang et al. 2018 general overlap estimates, Goenka et al. 2023 axial-symmetry results, and Chan–Hair 2025 algorithms for planar polygon translations; none entails the closed asymmetric-double-cone family formula without the new slice analysis. Actual semantic index searches produced related but non-covering results. Historical priority is provisional and no failure-to-find assertion is treated as proof of originality.
residual_risks: Fáry and Rédei (1950) and Grünbaum (1963) are related historical work cited by Stein; their complete texts were not materially inspected for exact unequal-apex bicone cases. A historically equivalent formula cannot be ruled out.
Specialized older or less-indexed literature on double cones, bipyramids, and the Macbeath region may contain an equivalent profile; the searchable database is not a complete priority oracle.
The 2025 polygon-overlap algorithm provides implicit computability for the two-dimensional subfamily, which is credited and is not claimed as new.
All novelty conclusions are self-review evaluations without an external independent audit.

value.rationale: The Kovner–Besicovitch/central-reflection volume ratio is an established natural affine-invariant shape functional. This finding determines the exact invariant, the explicit maximizing center, the full attainable interval, and a one-observable inverse of apex asymmetry for all positive dimensions and every centrally symmetric equator, including smooth and polyhedral bases. The universal base-shape cancellation is the structural point, and the fixed-parameter dimension limit gives a nontrivial asymptotic benchmark. The centroid discrepancy explains why centering at the centroid misses the optimal symmetric core. This is not a known universal uniqueness lemma, a mere renaming or an arbitrary small numerical improvement.
residual_risks: No claim of solving a general convex-body minimum or of a dimension-uniform inverse noise bound.
